subject: POC prompt collection spec & next steps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.inference.com>
To: Paula Reed <paula.reed@clarityhealth.com>, Jaspreet Singh <j.singh@clarityhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC prompt collection spec & next steps

Hi Paula / Jaspreet — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we have shared expectations for the POC prompt/log handoff.

POC goal (recap):
- Validate Redwood inference latency and quality on ClarityHealth triage assistant workload (diagnostic categorization + triage suggestions).
- Show unit-cost improvements with KV-caching and intelligent batching while preserving top-1/top-3 accuracy for the triage task.

Success criteria (proposal):
- Top-1 intent accuracy >= 88% on a held-out eval set provided by ClarityHealth.
- Latency 95th percentile < 420ms for single-turn requests at target concurrency.
- Per-token cost <= target in proposal (we'll verify after initial runs).

Evaluation plan / timing:
- Hand-off prompt/log bundle from Clarity by EOD 2027-06-03.
- Redwood prepares eval harness and runs baseline/optimized configs: 2027-06-04 through 2027-06-10.
- Joint review of results and signoff meeting: week of 2027-06-14.

Prompt/log requirements (what we need from Clarity):
1) Prompt set: 250–500 representative prompts in JSONL or CSV (one prompt per line). Include expected label(s) for each prompt when available.
2) Interaction logs: 3 business days of anonymized transcripts or token-level logs for the triage flows (CSV or JSONL). Columns we prefer: timestamp, user_id_hash, raw_text, system_decision_label, ground_truth_label (if available), metadata (flow_id).
3) A short manifest describing the distribution (e.g., % of triage categories) and any sampling biases.

Privacy & security notes:
- Do not include raw PHI. If you must share free-text containing PHI, please apply token-level redaction or replace named entities with placeholders (e.g., <PATIENT_NAME>, <DOB>).
- We can accept files via S3 presigned upload (we'll provide link) or a shared Drive folder. Files must be encrypted in transit.

Attachments I’m including: Redwood POC template (redwood_poc_template.xlsx) and our PII handling policy (clarity_poc_requirements.pdf). I’ll also send presigned upload instructions in a follow-up from Marissa.

Owners & actions:
- Clarity (Paula / Jaspreet): prepare prompt set + 3 days of logs; target delivery by 2027-06-03.
- Redwood (Marissa): provide presigned upload URL, data format checklist, and run initial ingestion.
- Redwood (Karthik): own success-criteria signoff + coordinate eval metrics and dashboard.

If that timeline looks good, confirm on this thread and Paula can drop the sample logs when ready. Happy to jump on a short follow-up if you want to align on anonymization rules.

Thanks —
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Vivek — this is helpful and the timeline works for us. A couple of quick clarifications before we package the files: 

1) For the interaction logs we have two export options: (a) raw transcripts (de-identified at source), or (b) token-level logs with model inputs/outputs and timing. Which is preferred for the baseline?
2) For redaction: is simple named-entity replacement acceptable (we have an internal script that maps names/IDs -> placeholders), or do you need hashing for user IDs?

I attached a 1MB snippet of yesterday's triage logs (clarity_sample_logs.csv) so you can confirm the schema. We’ll plan to run our de-id script and then upload the full bundle to the presigned link once we get it.

Also, can you confirm who on Redwood will have access to raw text (even if de-identified)? We need to document access for our security reviewers.

—Paula

On Sat, May 29, 2027 at 9:03 AM Paula Reed <paula.reed@clarityhealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks Vivek — this is helpful and the timeline works for us. A couple of quick clarifications before we package the files:
>
> 1) For the interaction logs we have two export options: (a) raw transcripts (de-identified at source), or (b) token-level logs with model inputs/outputs and timing. Which is preferred for the baseline?
> 2) For redaction: is simple named-entity replacement acceptable (we have an internal script that maps names/IDs -> placeholders), or do you need hashing for user IDs?

Hi Paula — thanks for the sample. Quick answers: 

- Preferred format: JSONL with one event per line (we also accept CSV). For prompt sets, JSONL with schema {"prompt_id","text","expected_label"} is ideal. Token-level logs are useful if you can provide them; timestamps and model output are valuable for latency profiling. If token-level is hard, raw transcripts + system decision label is fine for quality evals.

- Redaction: named-entity replacement (placeholders) is acceptable for POC ingestion. Hashing user IDs is preferred if you need a consistent pseudonym across sessions — include the hashing method in the manifest.

- Access controls: initially, evaluation will be performed by Marissa and the runtime team (redwood-inference@redwood.inference.com service account). We can scope access and provide a short-term project bucket with strict ACLs. We will not persist raw text beyond the agreed retention window (default 30 days) unless you authorize longer retention.

I’ve uploaded presigned upload instructions and a short checklist (redwood_presigned-upload-instructions.txt). Steps: we generate per-file presigned PUT URLs, you POST the files to the URLs, we validate checksums, then move to an isolated project bucket.

If you’re comfortable with placeholders for PHI, please run your de-id script and attach the manifest describing transformations. We’ll validate the schema on ingest and flag any missing columns.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_presigned-upload-instructions.txt
